subject.title: fix(cron): exclude lane waits from setup timeout

question: Should queued `cron-nested` admission be intentionally unbounded by the isolated-agent setup watchdog, with recovery owned by lane admission rather than cron setup timing?
rationale: The code change is mechanically narrow, but choosing which layer owns recovery from a lane wait determines whether stalled jobs fail visibly or remain pending; source tests alone cannot establish that operational contract.

options.title: Accept separate lane-wait ownership
options.body: Merge after runtime evidence demonstrates delayed admission succeeds and the lane subsystem has a bounded or otherwise reliable recovery path.

options.title: Retain a bounded queue-wait policy
options.body: Keep a separate, explicit admission-wait timeout if maintainers require cron jobs to fail rather than wait indefinitely when lane progress is lost.

recommendation.title: Accept separate lane-wait ownership
recommendation.body: Merge after runtime evidence demonstrates delayed admission succeeds and the lane subsystem has a bounded or otherwise reliable recovery path.
